Getting started¶

You need Python 3.13, Git, and MariaDB if you want to use the MariaDB option. SQLite is used by default, which is simpler when testing the project.

Windows PowerShell¶

Open a terminal in the folder with manage.py, then run:

py -3.13 -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
python manage.py migrate
python manage.py check
python manage.py test
python manage.py runserver

Visit http://127.0.0.1:8000/ to see the homepage.

To create an admin account, run python manage.py createsuperuser.

Make a file named .env only for the Docker Compose option. Never commit that file or share real passwords. See .env.example for the variables.

Local MariaDB¶

After creating a MariaDB database and a user, set these variables in the PowerShell terminal before running Django:

$env:DB_ENGINE = "mariadb"
$env:DB_NAME = "news_application"
$env:DB_USER = "news_user"
$env:DB_PASSWORD = "put-your-own-password-here"
$env:DB_HOST = "127.0.0.1"
$env:DB_PORT = "3306"
python manage.py migrate

Do not put the password in a Python file or into Git.
